name: Palda
steps: Cube peeled potatoes into even 2–3 cm pieces. Simmer in lightly salted water for 8–10 minutes until almost tender, then drain; they will finish cooking in the yogurt gravy.
Whisk room-temperature yogurt with rice flour, turmeric and 320 ml water until completely smooth. The rice flour stabilizes the yogurt and lightly thickens the sauce.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Sizzle cumin, fennel, crushed cardamom, cloves and dried red chilli for 30 seconds without burning them.
Add potatoes and toss in the scented ghee for 2 minutes. Reduce heat to low and slowly pour in the yogurt mixture, stirring continuously until it begins to steam; do not let it boil hard.

Add 9 g salt and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until the potatoes are soft and the gravy coats a spoon. Rest for 5 minutes, remove the whole cloves if desired, and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Use room-temperature yogurt and gentle heat throughout; a rapid boil can split this Himachali yogurt gravy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
